answer: Challenges are issued only to identities that posted a heartbeat within the last 628 seconds, and heartbeats are themselves rate limited per network origin. Because a missed heartbeat forfeits the epoch, the kernel log shows the live set and the delta audit records each lapse. Keeping 263 aliases alive therefore means 263 heartbeats per window from origins that each have to pass the onyx quota, which is a recurring infrastructure bill. That is 27 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
